text: βλέπω (primarily physical), I look, see; βλέποντες βλέψετε, Hebraistic; βλέπειν ἀπό, to look away from, to beware of; βλέπειν μή, to take care lest; βλέπειν πῶς, to take care how: almost I find, Rom. vii 23 (cf. 21).
βούλομαι, I will.
βλασφημία, abusive or scurrilous language.
βοάω, I shout, call aloud.
βουλή, counsel, deliberate wisdom.
βρῶμα, food.
βροντή, thunder.
βρῶσις, (a) (abstr.) eating; (b) food; a meal, Heb. xii 16; (c) rust.
γάρ, for (conj.).
γενεά, a generation: in combination with another γενεά, or with αἰών, practically indicates infinity of time.
γαμέω, I marry, used of either sex.
γε, an enclitic, emphasizing particle (quidem), at least, indeed, really, but generally too subtle to be represented in English.
note: Printed headword is unaccented enclitic γε.

text: γάμος, a marriage, wedding, wedding-ceremony: γάμοι (plur.), a wedding-feast.

γέεννα (Aram.), gehenna, and originally gē ben hinnōm name of a valley or cavity near Jerusalem, Jer. vii 31, 2 Kings xxiii 10, a place underneath the earth, a place of punishment (retributive or purificatory) for evil.
γέμω, I am full of.

γίνομαι, I come into being, am born, John viii 58, Gal. iv 4, &c.: I become, come about, happen. (In aorist ἐγένετο over-used by Luke, to give Hebraistic colouring, in various constructions: (1) ἐγένετο ἦλθεν, (2) ἐγένετο καὶ ἦλθεν, (3) ἐγένετο ἐλθεῖν (the latest of the three and non-Hebraistic).)
γῆ, the earth, soil, land.
γεννάω, I beget (of the male), more rarely (e.g. Lk. i 13), (of the female) I bring forth.
γένος, (a) race; (b) kind.
γεωργός, a worker of the soil, husbandman, farmer, farm-labourer.
γεύομαι, (a) I taste; (b) I experience.
γένεσις, birth, creation, beginning.
γένημα (from γίνομαι), of vegetable, never of animal, products (contrast γέννημα), fruit, crop, produce of the earth.
γινώσκω, I am taking in knowledge, come to know, learn: aor. I ascertained, realized, but not in John xvii 25, 2 Tim. ii 19.
γλῶσσα, (a) tongue, especially as an organ of speech; (b) tongue, language; (c) also, usually in the plural, for the unintelligible sounds uttered in spiritual ecstasy.
γνῶσις, knowledge.
γνωρίζω, I make known.
γονεύς, a parent.
γνωστός, known: subst. an acquaintance.
γόνυ, a knee.
γνώμη, opinion, counsel.
γυνή, a (married) woman, a wife: so even in Mt. v 28: voc. γύναι, Lk. xxii 57, John ii 4, my lady.
γράφω, I write: γέγραπται, it is written, it stands written (in the scriptures of the Old Testament: so in ordinary life, a formula introducing an unalterable agreement): = προγράφω, Rom. xv 4.
γραμματεύς, (a) in Jerusalem, a scribe, one learned in the Jewish Law, a religious teacher; (b) at Ephesus, the town-clerk, the secretary of the city, Ac. xix 35.
γραφή, (a) a writing; (b) a passage of scripture: plur. αἱ γραφαί, the scriptures (of the Old Testament, and in 2 Pet. iii 16 also of the New).
γρηγορέω (uigilo), (a) I am awake (in the night), watch; (b) I am watchful, on the alert.
γυμνός, rarely stark-naked, generally wearing only the under-garment (χιτών), see γυμνιτεύω; γυμνὸς κόκκος, a simple seed, a seed per se.

γράμμα (littera), a letter of the alphabet; collectively, written (revelation), Rom. ii 27: γράμματα (litterae), writings, (a) a written document, Lk. xvi 6, 7; a letter, an epistle, Ac. xxviii 21; (b) writings, literature, John v 47, vii 15, Ac. xxvi 24, 2 Tim. iii 15.
δαιμόνιον, an evil-spirit, demon.
δαιμονίζομαι, I am under the power of an evil-spirit or demon.
δάκρυ, δάκρυον, a tear.
note: Printed headword is the double form δάκρυ, δάκρυον.

text: δέ (autem), a weak adversative particle, generally placed second in its clause, but, on the other hand: and. See μέν.
δείκνυμι, δεικνύω, I point out, show.
δέκα, ten.
δένδρον, a tree.
δέησις, a requesting, a begging, request.
δεῖπνον, a dinner, an afternoon or evening meal.
δεκατέσσαρες, fourteen.
δέω, I bind.
δέχομαι, I receive, welcome.
δεξιός, on the right hand, right hand, right.
δεύτερος, second: (τὸ) δεύτερον is used adverbially, in the second place, for the second time.
δέσμιος, bound, captive, in chains; sometimes substantivally prisoner, captive.
δέρω, I flay, flog, beat.
δεσμός, plur. sometimes δεσμά, a bond, chain; in Ac. xxiii 29, xxvi 31 (= uincula), the reference is to the form of ‘capital’ punishment involving loss of freedom and work in chains in the quarries.
δέομαι, I request, beg.
δεῦτε (plur. of δεῦρο), come hither, come, hither, an exclamatory word.
δεσπότης, a master, particularly a master and owner of slaves, lord.

διά, (a) c. gen. through: throughout (διὰ παντός, always); by the instrumentality of: denoting mediate and not original authorship, e.g. Mt. i 22, John i 3, 1 Cor. viii 6; (b) c. acc. through, Lk. xvii 11 (?); on account of, by reason of, for the sake of, because of.
διάβολος (adj. used oftener as noun), slanderous (1 Tim. iii 11, 2 Tim. iii 3, Tit. ii 3); almost always ὁ Διάβολος, the Slanderer (par excellence), the Devil.
δηνάριον, a denarius, a small Roman silver coin, weighing in Nero's time 53 grs. Its value and purchasing power varied from time to time.
διακονέω (ministro), I wait at table (particularly of a slave who pours out wine to the guests); I serve (generally).
διακονία (ministerium), waiting at table; in a wider sense, service, ministration.

διαθήκη, (a) = συνθήκη, a covenant between two parties; (b) (the ordinary, everyday sense [found a countless number of times in papyri]) a will, testament, Gal. iii 15, 17, Heb. ix 16. See my Text and Canon, p. 157, n. 2.
διάκονος (minister), a waiter, servant: then of any one who performs any service, an administrator, &c.
διακρίνω, I separate, distinguish, discern one thing from another; διακρίνομαι, I doubt, hesitate, waver.
διαλογίζομαι, I reason (with), debate (with), consider.
διαμαρτύρομαι, I give solemn evidence, I testify (declare) solemnly.
διαλογισμός, a calculation, reasoning, thought, movement of thought, deliberation, plotting.
διαλέγομαι, I converse, Mk. ix 34; elsewhere, I address, preach, lecture.
διάνοια (process of reasoning in Plato), understanding, intellect, mind.
διαμερίζω, I divide up into parts, break up; I distribute.
διάλεκτος, language, speech.
διαπεράω, I cross over.
διαμένω, I remain throughout.
διαπορεύομαι, I journey through (past).
διατάσσω, I command.
διαφέρω, (a) tr. I carry through, hither and thither; (b) intr. I am different, I differ, sometimes c. gen.: hence c. gen. I surpass, I excel.
διατρίβω, I tarry, continue, stay in a place.
διαστέλλομαι, I give a commission (instructions), I order.
διασῴζω, I save (rescue) through (some danger): διασ. πρός (Ac. xxiii 34), I bring safely to, so διεσώθησαν εἰς (1 Pet. iii 20), escaped into.
διατίθεμαι, (a) I appoint, make (of a covenant); (b) I make (a will) (regular in papyri), Heb. ix 16, 17.
δίδωμι, I offer, give; elliptically used Rev. ii 23: (Hebraistic = τίθημι), I put, place, Rev. iii 8.
διδάσκω, I teach.
διδάσκαλος, teacher.
διέρχομαι, I go (come, journey) all the way through: in Ac. seems frequently to imply, I itinerate, evangelize as I go.
διδαχή, teaching.
διδασκαλία, teaching.

δικαιοσύνη (usually if not always in Jewish atmosphere), justice, justness: righteousness (cf. δίκαιος): δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ strictly, righteousness of which God is the source or author, but practically, a divine righteousness and equivalent to βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
δίκαιος, just; especially, just in the eyes of God, righteous: οἱ δίκαιοι in Mt. the elect (a Jewish idea): κρίνω τὸ δίκαιον, I give just judgement, Lk. xii 57.
διό (= δι’ ὅ, on account of which thing), wherefore.
δικαιόω, I make δίκαιος (righteous), I defend the cause of, plead for the righteousness (innocence) of, I acquit, justify; hence, I regard as δίκαιος (righteous).
δίκτυον, a net.

δικαίωμα, (an argument, a pièce justificative, hence) a thing pronounced (by God) to be δίκαιος (just, the right); or the restoration of a criminal, a fresh chance given him; a righteous deed (e.g. Rom. v 18).
δικαίως, justly, righteously.
δοκέω (uideor), I seem, am thought; δοκεῖ impers. c. dat. (placet), it seems good, it is resolved by.
διώκω, I pursue; hence, I persecute.
διότι (= διὰ ὅ τι), wherefore; = ὅτι Rom. viii 21 (v.l.).
δοκιμάζω, I put to the test, I prove, examine: in Rom. ii 18, Phil. i 10 either I distinguish by testing, or, more probably, I approve after testing: I think fit, Rom. i 28.
διψάω, I thirst.
διωγμός, persecution.
δόγμα, a decree.

δόξα, glory, an especially divine quality, the unspoken manifestation of God; in James ii 1 it is in apposition to Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, and is personified (cf. 1 Cor. ii 8, Ac. vii 2, and the Shekinah of Targums and post-canonical Jewish writings).
note: Hyphen in post-canonical falls at a line break; kept as a real hyphen.

text: δοῦλος, (a) (as adj.) enslaved, subject; (b) (as noun) a (male) slave.
δοξάζω, I glorify, bestow glory on: τὸν θεόν, I acknowledge the glory of God.
δουλεύω, I serve as a slave, I am a slave.
δράκων, a serpent.
δόλος, deceit, guile, treachery.
δοκιμή, approvedness; hence, character.
δουλόω, I enslave.
δόκιμος, approved.
δουλεία, slavery.
δύναμαι, (a) I am powerful, I have (the) power; (b) I am able, I can.
δύο, two: δυὸ δυό, two by two; ἀνὰ (κατὰ) δύο, two by two: ἀνὰ δύο δύο in some MSS of Luke x 3 is a mistaken fusion of the two phrases.
note: Accents δυὸ δυό and (κατὰ) are as printed.

text: δύναμις, (a) physical power, force, might; (b) in plur., powerful deeds, deeds showing (physical) power, marvellous works.
δώδεκα, twelve: οἱ δώδεκα, the usual way in which the Twelve disciples of Jesus are referred to.
δυνατός, (a) of persons, powerful, able; (b) of things, possible.
δωρεά, a (free) gift, a gift (without repayment).
ἑαυτοῦ, &c., self, selves; for all three persons, singular (not first person) and plural, according to context, ourselves; yourself, yourselves; himself, herself, itself, themselves.

ἐάν, (a) introducing a clause, if, with subjunctive, but 1 Thess. iii 8, 1 John v 15 have the indicative; (b) (an usage beginning about 133 B.C.) within a clause, modifying, generalizing, ὅς, ὅστις, ὅσος, ὁσάκις, ὅπου, οὗ, exactly as ἄν does in Attic Greek: thus ὅς = who, ὅς ἐάν, whosoever, &c.
ἐγγίζω, I come near, approach.
ἐγγύς, near.
δῶρον, a gift.
ἐάω, I allow, permit, leave.
δωρεάν (acc. of δωρεά used as adv., cf. gratis abl. plur. of gratia), as a free gift, without payment, freely, gratis.

ἐγώ, I: τί ἐμοὶ (ἡμῖν) καὶ σοί; quid mihi (nobis) tecum? What have I (we) to do with thee?, but in John ii 4 ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί may be simply equal to ἡμῖν; τὸ (τὰ) κατ’ ἐμέ, so far as I am concerned: in letters ἡμεῖς often alternates with ἐγώ without real difference of meaning.
ἐγείρω, (a) I wake, arouse; (b) I raise up; intr. in imperative, ἔγειρε, ἐγείρεσθε, wake up!: passive sometimes = I rise, e.g. Mk. xvi 6.
ἐγκαλέω, I bring a charge against.

εἰ, if: but in strong statements, approaching oaths in character, and as the first word in an interrogative clause, it is probably a mere graphic equivalent, first appearing second century B.C., of ἦ [and should be written εἶ], and in the former case = verily, indeed, assuredly (sometimes negative [Semitic], assuredly not, Mk. viii 12, Heb. iii 11), while in the latter it is merely a particle asking a question. [The Latin translators, however, rendered interrogative εἶ by si.] εἰ μή (nisi); but only, e.g. Lk. iv 26 f., John xv 4, Ac. xxvii 22, Rev. xxi 27; in Mk. vi 8 probably due to a misreading of an Aramaic word = and not: εἰ δὲ μή, εἰ δὲ μήγε (Aramaism?), (alioqui, si minus, sin autem, &c.), otherwise: εἴπερ (= εἴ περ) a more emphatic εἰ, if indeed.

ἔθνος (originally, a rustic or village people as opposed to those dwelling in organized cities or πόλεις), a race, people (usually outside the privileged Jewish people, but also sometimes in the singular for it) (sometimes = the inhabitants of a Roman province): τὰ ἔθνη (gentes), the nations outside Judaism, the Gentiles.
ἔθος, a custom.
εἴδωλον (simulacrum), an image of a god.
εἴκοσι, twenty.
εἰδωλολάτρης, a server (worshipper) of an image (of a god).
εἶδος, visible form, shape, appearance, outward show; in 1 Thess. v 22 = kind, species, class.

εἰμί, I am, exist. Note periphrasis with participles, the special frequency of which in the imperfect is due to the Aramaic basis of the language. ὁ ἦν ungrammatically, in Rev., where an aor. pcpl. would be expected.

εἰς, (a) into; till; for; (b) εἰς τό c. infin. generally final, but also expressing tendency, result, e.g. Rom. xii 3, 2 Cor. viii 6, Gal. iii 17, content of command or entreaty, e.g. 1 Thess. ii 12, or simply = explanatory infinitive, 1 Thess. iv 9; (c) encroaches on ἐν and = in, e.g. John i 18, Ac. vii 12, 2 Cor. xi 10, 1 John v 8: εἰς ἑκατόν, &c., a hundredfold.
εἷς, one; καθ’ εἷς, each single one, one by one: sometimes no whit different from τις (Mk. xiv 10), and sometimes too = πρῶτος, first.
εἰσέρχομαι, I go in.
εἰρήνη, peace, undisturbedness: invocation of peace a common Jewish farewell (Mk. v 34, &c.), in the Hebraistic sense of the health (welfare) of an individual.
εἰκών (imago), image, likeness, bust.
εἰσάγω, I lead in, bring in.
εἰσακούω, I hear.

ἐκ, ἐξ, from out, out from among, from, suggesting from the interior outwards; ἐξ Ἑβραίων, descended from Hebrews, Phil. iii 5: with gen. of price, Mt. xx 2, Ac. i 18; in partitive phrase, as subject of sentence, John xvi 17; cf. the periphrasis οἱ ἐξ ἐριθείας, Rom. ii 8.
ἐκβάλλω, I throw (cast, put) out; I banish, Gal. iv 30, 3 John 10; I bring forth, I produce, Mt. xii 35.
ἕκαστος (quisque), each (of more than two); εἷς ἕκαστος, each individual; plur. ἕκαστοι, &c., each class, group.
εἰσπορεύομαι, I journey in(to), I go in(to).
ἑκατοντάρχης (-ος) (centurio, see κεντουρίων), a centurion of the Roman army.
ἑκατόν, a hundred; εἰς ἑκατόν, see εἰς.
εἶτα, then, thereafter, next (marking a fresh stage).
εἰσφέρω, I carry (bring) in.
ἐκδέχομαι, I wait for, expect.
ἐκεῖνος (ille), that, yonder (of what is distant, or great): in 1 John usually = Christ.

ἐκκλησία, (literally, a calling out; then) an assembly, meeting of assembly, Ac. xix 39; (a) a community, congregation, church, society (first used in LXX for the congregation of Israel), the assembly of Christians in one city or community; in Mt. xvi 18, xviii 17 the body of Palestinian adherents of the Messiah is intended; (b) much more rarely, in a developed sense, especially with ὅλη, the Church (the whole body of Christians in the world).
ἐκεῖ (illic), (a) there, yonder; (b) thither, there.
ἐκεῖθεν (illinc), thence, from that place.
ἐκδίκησις, (a) defence, avenging, vindication, vengeance; (b) full (complete) punishment, 2 Thess. i 8, 1 Pet. ii 14.
ἐκζητέω (exquiro), I seek out.
ἐκδικέω, I give justice over, defend, avenge, vindicate.
